content: Weather tracker (issue 5) scope, 2026-09-17. Ori decided: NO provider rotation — every 5-min tick samples ALL providers, each gated by its own refresh properties (overrides issue 5 global one-request-slot wording). Local mongo host ports have no registry: 27017 qq-mongodb, 27018 data-refinery-mongo (and orphaned eidetic-mongo), 27019 jlab-mongodb; 27020 was free and is proposed for weather-mongodb. Sibling norm: dependencies=[] with pymongo in an optional extra, lazy-imported, exit 2 + install hint; no sibling containerises its poller (docker = data store only). Provider facts: open-meteo current is a 900 s model slice (~40 KB everything-request); met-no Expires ~30 min, ~62 KB fixed shape, needs identifying User-Agent; IMS token is a manual email grant (ims@ims.gov.il), timestamps are always UTC+2 despite +03:00 label, only source of measured solar radiation; OpenWeather free 2.5 needs 2 calls and lacks dew point/solar/UV; METAR LLSD is dead, LLBG works keyless. Frame: .devague weather-tracking-service, open questions q1-q7.

GitHub push protection on agentculture/climate-cli rejects a push (GH013) when ANY commit in it contains a string matching a provider key pattern, even an obvious placeholder: a 32-character fake OpenWeather appid literal in tests/weather/test_http.py blocked the whole feat/weather-tracking-service push on 2026-09-17. Fixing the file at the tip does not help, because the old blob stays in history - the only ways out are the per-push unblock URL (repo admin marks it as used-in-tests / false positive) or rewriting the unpushed history. Prevention: never write key-shaped literals in tests or docs; assemble fake secrets at runtime (e.g. join short words) and keep them visibly non-key-like. Brief task agents about this before they write redaction tests.

The Playwright MCP fails on the aarch64 Linux dev host: it defaults to --browser chrome, and Google Chrome has no Linux arm64 build (error: "Chromium distribution 'chrome' is not found at /opt/google/chrome/chrome"; `npx playwright install chrome` cannot fix it). Fix: configure the playwright MCP with --browser chromium (Playwright's own Chromium builds live in ~/.cache/ms-playwright). Workaround with no MCP restart: a standalone node script that requires playwright from the npx cache (~/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/playwright) and calls chromium.launch().

Recipe to browser-verify the dashboard's signed-out state and polling without waiting in real time: page.clock.install() before goto, then page.clock.runFor(61_000) to fire the 60 s poll; page.route('**/api/v1/**', r => r.fulfill({status: 302, headers: {location: ...}})) simulates an expired Cloudflare Access session (fetch uses redirect: 'manual', so it sees opaqueredirect); page.unroute simulates re-sign-in. Gotcha: after a click, waitForLoadState('networkidle') can return before refresh() reaches draw(), so the page-state banner still looks visible; wait ~2 s more before asserting.
